newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish purchasing managers' index rises in May.
newsitem.headline: Swedish purchasing managers' index rises in May.

text.p: Swedbank and I&L said on Monday their Swedish purchasing managers' index rose to 61.2 in May from 57.4 in April, showing the industrial economic trend improved further.
The May figure was the highest since the spring of 1995, Swedbank and I&L, a purchasers' association, said in a statement.
"The total index has strengthened gradually in the past year and it seems as if the economic upturn has gained speed," they said.

Swedbank and I&L noted that although an increase in stocks of material bought, to 54.1 from 50.3 in April, had a negative impact on the total index, they were not sure the rise had an adverse effect on economic trends.
"The handling of stocks has become more effective in past years and stock levels are generally lower," they said.
Industrial order intake was strong, mainly lifted by the export market.
Purchasing managers also remained optimistic about the future with the index for planned production over the next six months remaining just below 69 in May.
